title: Fast-WAM: Do World Action Models Need Test-time Future Imagination?
why: Absent mandatory initial architecture and deployment baseline. The proposed action-only QAT scope starts with Fast-WAM and must distinguish video co-training from its action-only inference path; this architecture anchor is needed before claiming a method for a class of WAMs.

title: SteerQuant: Steering Quantization Error with Action-Guided Scaling in World-Action Models
why: Absent mandatory recent WAM quantization comparator. Action-guided scaling is directly load-bearing for judging whether action-only QAT adds a distinct mechanism beyond directing quantization error according to its influence on actions.

title: QuantWAMs: Calibrating at the Right Granularity for World Action Models
why: Absent mandatory recent WAM PTQ comparator. Its calibration-granularity mechanism is needed to establish what action-only training changes beyond existing architecture-aware WAM quantization and to avoid treating a generic calibration transfer as novelty.

title: Q-WAM: 4-Bit Quantization of World Action Models with Action-Subspace Protection
why: Absent mandatory recent WAM quantization comparator. Action-subspace protection is a direct competing explanation for preserving low-bit actions, so the QAT proposal must distinguish its mechanism from this existing protection strategy.

title: Gated Relational Alignment via Confidence-based Distillation for Efficient VLMs
why: Absent mandatory GRACE comparator, whose exact arXiv identity is a VLM distillation work. Confidence-gated relational alignment supplies an adjacent teacher-distillation mechanism against which any claimed benefit beyond matched teacher distillation must be distinguished; it is not evidence of WAM QAT.

title: EfficientDM: Efficient Quantization-Aware Fine-Tuning of Low-Bit Diffusion Models
why: Absent mandatory older explicit QAT baseline. Although outside the preferred last-12-month window, efficient quantization-aware fine-tuning of low-bit diffusion models is a load-bearing baseline for determining whether action-only WAM QAT improves on ordinary diffusion QAT rather than merely transplanting it.

title: QVGen: Pushing the Limit of Quantized Video Generative Models
why: Absent mandatory older explicit QAT baseline. It is an adjacent video QAT comparator outside the preferred last-12-month window, retained because the user explicitly requires separating a WAM action-only mechanism from generic video QAT transplantation; video generation results do not establish robot-control benefit.

title: Causal World Modeling for Robot Control
why: Absent mandatory LingBot-VA extension architecture. This baseline is load-bearing for the requested cross-architecture WAM scope, including the distinction between the released shared-backbone variant and the paper's separate-expert variant when defining action-only quantization and training boundaries.

title: Cosmos Policy: Fine-Tuning Video Models for Visuomotor Control and Planning
why: Absent mandatory Cosmos Policy extension architecture. Its shared generator and action-token pathway is needed to test whether the proposed action-only QAT definition generalizes beyond a separate ActionDiT and to make architecture-dependent training scope explicit.

title: Flash-WAM: Modality-Aware Distillation for World Action Models
why: Absent mandatory recent adjacent WAM distillation comparator. Modality-aware distillation is needed to separate any action-only QAT contribution from teacher-driven WAM compression or acceleration; Flash-WAM is a distillation work, not QAT.
